levels.title: Research an Appropriate Client Fit
levels.objective: Practice research an appropriate client fit in a realistic client relationship using ethical, evidence-based decisions.
levels.teaching: A suitable lead is one whose actual needs match the offered service and capacity. Worked example: A small design agency discovers a prospect needs an audited construction blueprint, outside its services. The appropriate response is to explain the service boundary and refer to a suitable qualified provider instead of selling a mismatch. Avoid promise professional engineering certification without capability and hide limitations until after payment.
levels.workedExample: Client context: A small design agency discovers a prospect needs an audited construction blueprint, outside its services. Example decision: Explain the service boundary and refer to a suitable qualified provider instead of selling a mismatch.
levels.commonMistake: Promise professional engineering certification without capability
levels.remediation: A mismatch is not a sales opportunity to force.
levels.hint: Use this business principle: A suitable lead is one whose actual needs match the offered service and capacity.

challenges.prompt: In "Research an Appropriate Client Fit", a realistic client situation occurs: A small design agency discovers a prospect needs an audited construction blueprint, outside its services. Which response matches good sales practice?

options.a: Explain the service boundary and refer to a suitable qualified provider instead of selling a mismatch
options.b: Promise professional engineering certification without capability
options.c: Hide limitations until after payment

challenges.feedback: A suitable lead is one whose actual needs match the offered service and capacity. Recommended response: Explain the service boundary and refer to a suitable qualified provider instead of selling a mismatch.

challenges.prompt: A consultant is advising a freelance video editor choosing which enquiries merit discovery calls. Which action best protects a clear and ethical client relationship?

options.a: Promise every enquiry delivery within twenty-four hours
options.b: Qualify leads by checking video requirements, client objectives, footage rights and editing capacity
options.c: Accept a specialist animation project without the required skills

challenges.feedback: Qualify leads by checking video requirements, client objectives, footage rights and editing capacity. A mismatch is not a sales opportunity to force.

challenges.prompt: Consider this claim in the context of "Research an Appropriate Client Fit": Researching fit before pitching can protect both a buyer's budget and a seller's reputation.
challenges.feedback: A mismatch is not a sales opportunity to force.

levels.title: Open a Respectful Discovery Conversation
levels.objective: Practice open a respectful discovery conversation in a realistic client relationship using ethical, evidence-based decisions.
levels.teaching: A consultation should gain permission, explain purpose and invite the client's priorities. Worked example: A client attends a first call about improving a small restaurant's social posts. The appropriate response is to ask permission to understand their goals before recommending packages. Avoid start with a five-minute monologue about agency awards and demand a payment commitment before discussing needs.
levels.workedExample: Client context: A client attends a first call about improving a small restaurant's social posts. Example decision: Ask permission to understand their goals before recommending packages.
levels.commonMistake: Start with a five-minute monologue about agency awards
levels.remediation: Respectful questions reveal genuine needs.
levels.hint: Use this business principle: A consultation should gain permission, explain purpose and invite the client's priorities.

challenges.prompt: In "Open a Respectful Discovery Conversation", a realistic client situation occurs: A client attends a first call about improving a small restaurant's social posts. Which response matches good sales practice?

options.a: Demand a payment commitment before discussing needs
options.b: Ask permission to understand their goals before recommending packages
options.c: Start with a five-minute monologue about agency awards

challenges.feedback: A consultation should gain permission, explain purpose and invite the client's priorities. Recommended response: Ask permission to understand their goals before recommending packages.

challenges.prompt: A consultant is advising a web consultant beginning a call with a potential school client. Which action best protects a clear and ethical client relationship?

options.a: Ask permission to explore the school's goals, current site issues and decision process
options.b: Begin with an unbroken pitch about agency awards
options.c: Demand the full contract signature before asking questions

challenges.feedback: Ask permission to explore the school's goals, current site issues and decision process. Respectful questions reveal genuine needs.

challenges.prompt: Consider this claim in the context of "Open a Respectful Discovery Conversation": An effective discovery call requires dominating the conversation to establish authority.
challenges.feedback: Respectful questions reveal genuine needs.

levels.title: Ask Specific Needs Questions
levels.objective: Practice ask specific needs questions in a realistic client relationship using ethical, evidence-based decisions.
levels.teaching: Open questions and practical follow-ups uncover constraints better than vague satisfaction ratings. Worked example: A shop owner says they want "more online growth" but cannot define success. The appropriate response is to ask which customer action, channel and time window would count as progress. Avoid assume the owner wants ten thousand followers and offer a fixed ad budget without asking about sales capacity.
levels.workedExample: Client context: A shop owner says they want "more online growth" but cannot define success. Example decision: Ask which customer action, channel and time window would count as progress.
levels.commonMistake: Assume the owner wants ten thousand followers
levels.remediation: The answer should shape the actual proposal.
levels.hint: Use this business principle: Open questions and practical follow-ups uncover constraints better than vague satisfaction ratings.

challenges.prompt: In "Ask Specific Needs Questions", a realistic client situation occurs: A shop owner says they want "more online growth" but cannot define success. Which response matches good sales practice?

options.a: Assume the owner wants ten thousand followers
options.b: Offer a fixed ad budget without asking about sales capacity
options.c: Ask which customer action, channel and time window would count as progress

challenges.feedback: Open questions and practical follow-ups uncover constraints better than vague satisfaction ratings. Recommended response: Ask which customer action, channel and time window would count as progress.

challenges.prompt: A consultant is advising a consultancy clarifying what "better reporting" means to an operations manager. Which action best protects a clear and ethical client relationship?

options.a: Assume better reporting means new dashboard colors
options.b: Quote a complete BI platform without checking required metrics
options.c: Ask which report users, decisions, data sources and time window the client needs

challenges.feedback: Ask which report users, decisions, data sources and time window the client needs. The answer should shape the actual proposal.

challenges.prompt: Consider this claim in the context of "Ask Specific Needs Questions": Specific questions can expose the underlying business outcome behind a vague request.
challenges.feedback: The answer should shape the actual proposal.

levels.title: Confirm Decision Criteria
levels.objective: Practice confirm decision criteria in a realistic client relationship using ethical, evidence-based decisions.
levels.teaching: Before proposing, identify budget boundaries, schedule, approval roles and expected results. Worked example: A client says the project must be approved by a partner and ready before a planned event. The appropriate response is to confirm the approver, decision date, usable budget range and nonnegotiable deliverables. Avoid promise to begin without discussing approval and ignore the event date until contract signature.
levels.workedExample: Client context: A client says the project must be approved by a partner and ready before a planned event. Example decision: Confirm the approver, decision date, usable budget range and nonnegotiable deliverables.
levels.commonMistake: Promise to begin without discussing approval
levels.remediation: Timing, risk, authority and deliverables also matter.
levels.hint: Use this business principle: Before proposing, identify budget boundaries, schedule, approval roles and expected results.

challenges.prompt: In "Confirm Decision Criteria", a realistic client situation occurs: A client says the project must be approved by a partner and ready before a planned event. Which response matches good sales practice?

options.a: Confirm the approver, decision date, usable budget range and nonnegotiable deliverables
options.b: Promise to begin without discussing approval
options.c: Ignore the event date until contract signature

challenges.feedback: Before proposing, identify budget boundaries, schedule, approval roles and expected results. Recommended response: Confirm the approver, decision date, usable budget range and nonnegotiable deliverables.

challenges.prompt: A consultant is advising a café owner asking for content work before launch. Which action best protects a clear and ethical client relationship?

options.a: Treat a vague interest message as acceptance of the most expensive package
options.b: Confirm launch date, available assets, approvals and the actual campaign outcome before offering scope
options.c: Commit to a launch date before seeing any product imagery

challenges.feedback: Confirm launch date, available assets, approvals and the actual campaign outcome before offering scope. Timing, risk, authority and deliverables also matter.

levels.title: Summarize a Client's Actual Request
levels.objective: Practice summarize a client's actual request in a realistic client relationship using ethical, evidence-based decisions.
levels.teaching: A written recap should separate confirmed requirements from suggestions and assumptions. Worked example: After discovery, a manager hears "six edited clips and product photos within two weeks". The appropriate response is to send a concise recap of six clips, photos, deadline and questions awaiting confirmation. Avoid change the number of clips to ten without asking and describe an unrequested website rebuild as approved work.
levels.workedExample: Client context: After discovery, a manager hears "six edited clips and product photos within two weeks". Example decision: Send a concise recap of six clips, photos, deadline and questions awaiting confirmation.
levels.commonMistake: Change the number of clips to ten without asking
levels.remediation: Recaps prevent avoidable scope disputes.
levels.hint: Use this business principle: A written recap should separate confirmed requirements from suggestions and assumptions.

challenges.prompt: In "Summarize a Client's Actual Request", a realistic client situation occurs: After discovery, a manager hears "six edited clips and product photos within two weeks". Which response matches good sales practice?

options.a: Describe an unrequested website rebuild as approved work
options.b: Send a concise recap of six clips, photos, deadline and questions awaiting confirmation
options.c: Change the number of clips to ten without asking

challenges.feedback: A written recap should separate confirmed requirements from suggestions and assumptions. Recommended response: Send a concise recap of six clips, photos, deadline and questions awaiting confirmation.

challenges.prompt: A consultant is advising a consultant following up after a nonprofit's planning call. Which action best protects a clear and ethical client relationship?

options.a: Send a factual recap distinguishing confirmed goals, suggested work and unresolved questions
options.b: Present unrequested services as fully approved
options.c: Invent the client's budget when drafting the recap

challenges.feedback: Send a factual recap distinguishing confirmed goals, suggested work and unresolved questions. Recaps prevent avoidable scope disputes.

challenges.feedback: Recaps prevent avoidable scope disputes.

levels.title: Checkpoint: Prepare a Discovery Script
levels.objective: Practice checkpoint: prepare a discovery script in a realistic client relationship using ethical, evidence-based decisions.
levels.teaching: A discovery guide should progress from goals to current situation, constraints and agreed next step. Worked example: A fictional tutoring academy seeks help getting more qualified admission enquiries. The appropriate response is to prepare questions on audience, channels, enquiry quality, response capacity, timing and approval. Avoid use only "How big is your budget?" as the consultation and promise enrolment volumes before examining prior data.
levels.workedExample: Client context: A fictional tutoring academy seeks help getting more qualified admission enquiries. Example decision: Prepare questions on audience, channels, enquiry quality, response capacity, timing and approval.
levels.commonMistake: Use only "How big is your budget?" as the consultation
levels.remediation: Discovery is not a memorized pressure pitch.
levels.hint: Use this business principle: A discovery guide should progress from goals to current situation, constraints and agreed next step.

challenges.prompt: In "Checkpoint: Prepare a Discovery Script", a realistic client situation occurs: A fictional tutoring academy seeks help getting more qualified admission enquiries. Which response matches good sales practice?

options.a: Use only "How big is your budget?" as the consultation
options.b: Promise enrolment volumes before examining prior data
options.c: Prepare questions on audience, channels, enquiry quality, response capacity, timing and approval

challenges.feedback: A discovery guide should progress from goals to current situation, constraints and agreed next step. Recommended response: Prepare questions on audience, channels, enquiry quality, response capacity, timing and approval.

challenges.prompt: A consultant is advising a freelancer preparing a 15-minute introductory service call. Which action best protects a clear and ethical client relationship?

options.a: Spend all fifteen minutes describing one's own portfolio
options.b: Guarantee a sales return before knowing the prospect's market
options.c: Prepare goals, qualification questions, scope boundaries and a specific next step for a short call

challenges.feedback: Prepare goals, qualification questions, scope boundaries and a specific next step for a short call. Discovery is not a memorized pressure pitch.

challenges.prompt: Consider this claim in the context of "Checkpoint: Prepare a Discovery Script": A good script leaves space for client answers and a confirmed next step.
challenges.feedback: Discovery is not a memorized pressure pitch.

levels.title: Describe Scope and Deliverables Clearly
levels.objective: Practice describe scope and deliverables clearly in a realistic client relationship using ethical, evidence-based decisions.
levels.teaching: Deliverables should specify quantities, formats, channels, timing and who provides input. Worked example: A package lists "social media management" but says nothing about posts or revisions. The appropriate response is to specify monthly assets, approval rounds, platform responsibilities and deliverable formats. Avoid assume unlimited content is included under vague wording and hide the need for brand assets from the client.
levels.workedExample: Client context: A package lists "social media management" but says nothing about posts or revisions. Example decision: Specify monthly assets, approval rounds, platform responsibilities and deliverable formats.
levels.commonMistake: Assume unlimited content is included under vague wording
levels.remediation: Outputs and responsibilities reduce ambiguity.
levels.hint: Use this business principle: Deliverables should specify quantities, formats, channels, timing and who provides input.

challenges.prompt: In "Describe Scope and Deliverables Clearly", a realistic client situation occurs: A package lists "social media management" but says nothing about posts or revisions. Which response matches good sales practice?

options.a: Specify monthly assets, approval rounds, platform responsibilities and deliverable formats
options.b: Assume unlimited content is included under vague wording
options.c: Hide the need for brand assets from the client

challenges.feedback: Deliverables should specify quantities, formats, channels, timing and who provides input. Recommended response: Specify monthly assets, approval rounds, platform responsibilities and deliverable formats.

challenges.prompt: A consultant is advising a small media agency defining a four-video content package. Which action best protects a clear and ethical client relationship?

options.a: Add filming to the quote without obtaining pricing consent
options.b: List exactly four edits, source-footage obligations, file formats, turnaround and revision limit
options.c: Describe the package as unlimited full-service production

challenges.feedback: List exactly four edits, source-footage obligations, file formats, turnaround and revision limit. Outputs and responsibilities reduce ambiguity.

challenges.prompt: Consider this claim in the context of "Describe Scope and Deliverables Clearly": A statement of work becomes clearer when it identifies outputs rather than only activities.
challenges.feedback: Outputs and responsibilities reduce ambiguity.

levels.title: Estimate Effort and Dependencies
levels.objective: Practice estimate effort and dependencies in a realistic client relationship using ethical, evidence-based decisions.
levels.teaching: Schedules should account for input collection, approvals, production and revisions. Worked example: A site requires client-provided product images before pages can be built. The appropriate response is to show the image deadline and a dependent build milestone with review time. Avoid promise a finished site before the client can supply content and remove approvals from the schedule to appear faster.
levels.workedExample: Client context: A site requires client-provided product images before pages can be built. Example decision: Show the image deadline and a dependent build milestone with review time.
levels.commonMistake: Promise a finished site before the client can supply content
levels.remediation: Work cannot complete before required inputs and sign-offs.
levels.hint: Use this business principle: Schedules should account for input collection, approvals, production and revisions.

challenges.prompt: In "Estimate Effort and Dependencies", a realistic client situation occurs: A site requires client-provided product images before pages can be built. Which response matches good sales practice?

options.a: Remove approvals from the schedule to appear faster
options.b: Show the image deadline and a dependent build milestone with review time
options.c: Promise a finished site before the client can supply content

challenges.feedback: Schedules should account for input collection, approvals, production and revisions. Recommended response: Show the image deadline and a dependent build milestone with review time.

challenges.prompt: A consultant is advising a graphic designer building a campaign calendar for a brand. Which action best protects a clear and ethical client relationship?

options.a: Map content handover, shoot availability, brand approval and revision buffers on the calendar
options.b: Promise publication before client-provided assets arrive
options.c: Ignore the owner's scheduled review week

challenges.feedback: Map content handover, shoot availability, brand approval and revision buffers on the calendar. Work cannot complete before required inputs and sign-offs.

challenges.feedback: Work cannot complete before required inputs and sign-offs.

levels.title: Explain Pricing Assumptions
levels.objective: Practice explain pricing assumptions in a realistic client relationship using ethical, evidence-based decisions.
levels.teaching: An ethical quote makes scope, units, taxes, payment timing and exclusions understandable. Worked example: A fictional shoot costs PKR 40,000 before separately priced venue hire. The appropriate response is to label the shoot fee and make venue rental a visible optional cost. Avoid describe the base fee as fully inclusive when it is not and add an undisclosed production charge after acceptance.
levels.workedExample: Client context: A fictional shoot costs PKR 40,000 before separately priced venue hire. Example decision: Label the shoot fee and make venue rental a visible optional cost.
levels.commonMistake: Describe the base fee as fully inclusive when it is not
levels.remediation: Hidden costs undermine informed consent.
levels.hint: Use this business principle: An ethical quote makes scope, units, taxes, payment timing and exclusions understandable.

challenges.prompt: In "Explain Pricing Assumptions", a realistic client situation occurs: A fictional shoot costs PKR 40,000 before separately priced venue hire. Which response matches good sales practice?

options.a: Describe the base fee as fully inclusive when it is not
options.b: Add an undisclosed production charge after acceptance
options.c: Label the shoot fee and make venue rental a visible optional cost

challenges.feedback: An ethical quote makes scope, units, taxes, payment timing and exclusions understandable. Recommended response: Label the shoot fee and make venue rental a visible optional cost.

challenges.prompt: A consultant is advising a content agency quoting a monthly retainer and paid media spend. Which action best protects a clear and ethical client relationship?

options.a: Present the retainer as including unlimited advertising budget
options.b: Add an undisclosed media fee after approval
options.c: Separate agency retainer, tax assumptions, client ad spend and any optional production costs

challenges.feedback: Separate agency retainer, tax assumptions, client ad spend and any optional production costs. Hidden costs undermine informed consent.

challenges.prompt: Consider this claim in the context of "Explain Pricing Assumptions": A transparent price should distinguish service fees from third-party expenses.
challenges.feedback: Hidden costs undermine informed consent.

levels.title: Compare Proposals Transparently
levels.objective: Practice compare proposals transparently in a realistic client relationship using ethical, evidence-based decisions.
levels.teaching: Package choices should use a consistent set of comparison criteria and disclose limitations. Worked example: A client compares four short videos versus eight videos with an extra review cycle. The appropriate response is to show both options with volume, turnaround, revisions, client inputs and exclusions. Avoid call the larger package better without comparing fit and invent features to make the cheaper option look inferior.
levels.workedExample: Client context: A client compares four short videos versus eight videos with an extra review cycle. Example decision: Show both options with volume, turnaround, revisions, client inputs and exclusions.
levels.commonMistake: Call the larger package better without comparing fit
levels.remediation: Clarity helps clients choose what they actually need.
levels.hint: Use this business principle: Package choices should use a consistent set of comparison criteria and disclose limitations.

challenges.prompt: In "Compare Proposals Transparently", a realistic client situation occurs: A client compares four short videos versus eight videos with an extra review cycle. Which response matches good sales practice?

options.a: Show both options with volume, turnaround, revisions, client inputs and exclusions
options.b: Call the larger package better without comparing fit
options.c: Invent features to make the cheaper option look inferior

challenges.feedback: Package choices should use a consistent set of comparison criteria and disclose limitations. Recommended response: Show both options with volume, turnaround, revisions, client inputs and exclusions.

challenges.prompt: A consultant is advising a marketing consultancy presenting a basic and premium scope. Which action best protects a clear and ethical client relationship?

options.a: Invent scarcity to pressure the buyer into upgrading
options.b: Use one comparison table showing volumes, deliverables, turnaround, reviews and exclusions for both options
options.c: Describe the premium option as better without explaining the difference

challenges.feedback: Use one comparison table showing volumes, deliverables, turnaround, reviews and exclusions for both options. Clarity helps clients choose what they actually need.

challenges.prompt: Consider this claim in the context of "Compare Proposals Transparently": Different packages are easier to evaluate when compared against the same criteria.
challenges.feedback: Clarity helps clients choose what they actually need.

levels.title: Specify Exclusions and Revision Limits
levels.objective: Practice specify exclusions and revision limits in a realistic client relationship using ethical, evidence-based decisions.
levels.teaching: Contracts should identify out-of-scope work and a fair method for handling changes. Worked example: A monthly design package includes two revision rounds but a client requests a full campaign reshoot. The appropriate response is to explain the agreed revisions and offer a separately scoped reshoot estimate. Avoid claim the reshoot is free then surprise the client with charges and reject all feedback even within the agreed rounds.
levels.workedExample: Client context: A monthly design package includes two revision rounds but a client requests a full campaign reshoot. Example decision: Explain the agreed revisions and offer a separately scoped reshoot estimate.
levels.commonMistake: Claim the reshoot is free then surprise the client with charges
levels.remediation: Clear boundaries protect the relationship.
levels.hint: Use this business principle: Contracts should identify out-of-scope work and a fair method for handling changes.

challenges.prompt: In "Specify Exclusions and Revision Limits", a realistic client situation occurs: A monthly design package includes two revision rounds but a client requests a full campaign reshoot. Which response matches good sales practice?

options.a: Reject all feedback even within the agreed rounds
options.b: Explain the agreed revisions and offer a separately scoped reshoot estimate
options.c: Claim the reshoot is free then surprise the client with charges

challenges.feedback: Contracts should identify out-of-scope work and a fair method for handling changes. Recommended response: Explain the agreed revisions and offer a separately scoped reshoot estimate.

challenges.prompt: A consultant is advising a video editor defining whether subtitles and extra formats are included. Which action best protects a clear and ethical client relationship?

options.a: Confirm whether subtitles and aspect-ratio exports are included and record any extra rate in advance

challenges.prompt: Consider this claim in the context of "Specify Exclusions and Revision Limits": Revision limits should be stated before work begins and applied consistently.
challenges.feedback: Clear boundaries protect the relationship.

levels.title: Checkpoint: Write a Two-Option Offer
levels.objective: Practice checkpoint: write a two-option offer in a realistic client relationship using ethical, evidence-based decisions.
levels.teaching: Two offers should solve the same client goal at different levels of scope without imaginary savings. Worked example: A small clinic needs appointment explainer content and only modest production capacity. The appropriate response is to offer a compact and expanded content package with exact assets, review windows and exclusions. Avoid advertise guaranteed bookings from either option and put every important detail in an unreadable footnote.
levels.workedExample: Client context: A small clinic needs appointment explainer content and only modest production capacity. Example decision: Offer a compact and expanded content package with exact assets, review windows and exclusions.
levels.commonMistake: Advertise guaranteed bookings from either option
levels.remediation: Transparency matters more than upselling.
levels.hint: Use this business principle: Two offers should solve the same client goal at different levels of scope without imaginary savings.

options.a: Advertise guaranteed bookings from either option
options.b: Put every important detail in an unreadable footnote
options.c: Offer a compact and expanded content package with exact assets, review windows and exclusions

challenges.feedback: Two offers should solve the same client goal at different levels of scope without imaginary savings. Recommended response: Offer a compact and expanded content package with exact assets, review windows and exclusions.

options.c: Offer two clearly scoped launch bundles with specific quantities, revisions, dependencies and exclusions

challenges.prompt: Consider this claim in the context of "Checkpoint: Write a Two-Option Offer": Two clear offers can help a client trade scope against budget without pressure.

levels.title: Handle a Budget Concern Calmly
levels.objective: Practice handle a budget concern calmly in a realistic client relationship using ethical, evidence-based decisions.
levels.teaching: When price is challenged, investigate the constraint and explore legitimate scope changes. Worked example: A client says a PKR 100,000 quote exceeds the available budget. The appropriate response is to ask which outcomes matter most and propose a smaller scope with its limitations explained. Avoid pressure the client to borrow money immediately and promise the entire original scope at an unsustainable fee.
levels.workedExample: Client context: A client says a PKR 100,000 quote exceeds the available budget. Example decision: Ask which outcomes matter most and propose a smaller scope with its limitations explained.
levels.commonMistake: Pressure the client to borrow money immediately
levels.remediation: Scope, timing and priorities may matter more than discounting.
levels.hint: Use this business principle: When price is challenged, investigate the constraint and explore legitimate scope changes.

challenges.prompt: In "Handle a Budget Concern Calmly", a realistic client situation occurs: A client says a PKR 100,000 quote exceeds the available budget. Which response matches good sales practice?

options.a: Ask which outcomes matter most and propose a smaller scope with its limitations explained
options.b: Pressure the client to borrow money immediately
options.c: Promise the entire original scope at an unsustainable fee

challenges.feedback: When price is challenged, investigate the constraint and explore legitimate scope changes. Recommended response: Ask which outcomes matter most and propose a smaller scope with its limitations explained.

challenges.prompt: A consultant is advising a designer negotiating an optional photography day. Which action best protects a clear and ethical client relationship?

options.a: Promise to include extra shooting for no fee without resource review
options.b: Ask about the budget cap and offer photography as an optional separated deliverable or phased work

challenges.feedback: Scope, timing and priorities may matter more than discounting.

levels.title: Respond to a Scope-Creep Request
levels.objective: Practice respond to a scope-creep request in a realistic client relationship using ethical, evidence-based decisions.
levels.teaching: Unplanned deliverables should be assessed against agreed scope, timeline and fair pricing. Worked example: A client adds six video edits after approving a contract for four. The appropriate response is to document the six extra edits and offer a change order with timeline impact. Avoid do the extra work without updating any expectation and refuse the entire project instead of discussing options.
levels.workedExample: Client context: A client adds six video edits after approving a contract for four. Example decision: Document the six extra edits and offer a change order with timeline impact.
levels.commonMistake: Do the extra work without updating any expectation
levels.remediation: An agreed change order records the new trade-off.
levels.hint: Use this business principle: Unplanned deliverables should be assessed against agreed scope, timeline and fair pricing.

challenges.prompt: In "Respond to a Scope-Creep Request", a realistic client situation occurs: A client adds six video edits after approving a contract for four. Which response matches good sales practice?

options.a: Refuse the entire project instead of discussing options
options.b: Document the six extra edits and offer a change order with timeline impact
options.c: Do the extra work without updating any expectation

challenges.feedback: Unplanned deliverables should be assessed against agreed scope, timeline and fair pricing. Recommended response: Document the six extra edits and offer a change order with timeline impact.

challenges.prompt: A consultant is advising a software consultancy asked to add new pages to an approved website scope. Which action best protects a clear and ethical client relationship?

levels.title: Explain a Realistic Deadline
levels.objective: Practice explain a realistic deadline in a realistic client relationship using ethical, evidence-based decisions.
levels.teaching: Delivery dates should include known dependencies, review buffers and uncertainty. The appropriate response is to explain the production lead time and offer a feasible reduced scope or later delivery date. Avoid say yes while planning to miss the deadline and skip safety and quality checks without consent.

levels.commonMistake: Say yes while planning to miss the deadline
levels.remediation: Overpromising creates reputational and operational harm.
levels.hint: Use this business principle: Delivery dates should include known dependencies, review buffers and uncertainty.

options.a: Say yes while planning to miss the deadline
options.b: Skip safety and quality checks without consent
options.c: Explain the production lead time and offer a feasible reduced scope or later delivery date

challenges.feedback: Delivery dates should include known dependencies, review buffers and uncertainty. Recommended response: Explain the production lead time and offer a feasible reduced scope or later delivery date.

challenges.prompt: A consultant is advising a web studio planning a site launch after payment gateway approval. Which action best protects a clear and ethical client relationship?

levels.title: Know When to Decline a Bad Fit
